messages:
ryan: Heads-up — new Dedicated customer wants BYOK with split custody (customer HSM + Redwood wrap). They also asked for explicit RBAC controls, audit forwarding to their SIEM, and SOC2 evidence. Quick sanity-check: what are the key custody boundaries we should commit to and where do we draw the line for Redwood access?

michelle: +1 need clarity. From compliance POV we can host a key-wrapping KMS in our VPC while customer-held HSM stores root key. But we need to document who can request key unwrap actions and how they’re logged.

anika: For Dedicated we usually do envelope encryption: customer root in their HSM -> wrap keys via KMIP/PKCS11 or AWS KMS external key -> store wrapped DEKs in our DB. That keeps raw key material out of our env.

dave: Practically, customers want emergency escrow/rotation assistance. We should define an escalation playbook (who gets access, for how long, approvals). Also: require JIT access via Vault with short TTLs.

kate: Oncall: any RBAC change that touches key_admin or key_operator roles => must trigger a review workflow and create an immutable audit event with diff + approver. We can forward to their SIEM via syslog/HTTPS. Retention must meet customer requirements (default 1y, option to extend).

michelle: Compliance constraints: SOC2/ISO/PCI expect separation of duties and audited break-glass. We can offer split-role model: key_admin (customer-managed by default), key_operator (Redwood limited ops), auditor (read-only log access). Require MFA + access justification.

ryan: For RBAC, propose minimal roles: ["key_viewer", "key_operator", "key_admin", "key_auditor", "oncall"] with least privilege. Can we show a sample policy snippet?

michelle: Example policy (pseudo JSON):
```
{
  "role": "key_operator",
  "capabilities": ["unwrap_dek", "rotate_wrapped_dek"],
  "conditions": {"mfa": true, "session_ttl": "15m", "justification_required": true}
}
```

anika: Also note: unwrap_dek should be gated by a hardware attestation check if available and only allow for ephemeral session keys. We shouldn't allow permanent plaintext DEKs in Redwood memory beyond request lifetime.

dave: Vulnerability/incident angle: if we detect suspicious activity (multiple unwrap attempts, failed attestation), auto-lock the key and create an incident in the IR playbook. That playbook needs clear owner (security oncall + customer contact).

kate: +1. Logging details: every unwrap/rotate/escrow action must produce an audit record with: actor, role, reason, request_id, source_ip, mfa_ok, attestation_result, and a hash of the wrapped key blob. Forward to customer SIEM and our internal audit index.

ryan: Question about KMS integration: customers on Azure/AWS/GCP — do we support direct external KMS (EKMS) or only HSM-backed PKCS11? There’s also attestation differences across clouds.

anika: We support both patterns but for BYOK we recommend HSM/PKCS11 for on-prem, and EKMS with external key material (imported key) for cloud. Need to capture attestation artifact: cert chain or KMS attestation token.

michelle: Compliance note: when customers supply key material to a cloud KMS, we still need explicit contract clauses for custody and evidence of key destruction on termination. Add that to the contract template.

ryan: Action items?

michelle: 1) Draft RBAC role definitions + sample policy snippets (owner: michelle)
2) Draft audit event schema + retention options and SIEM forwarding config (owner: kate)
3) Define JIT access flow using Vault + attestation gating (owner: anika)
4) Escrow & break-glass playbook + legal contract wording for BYOK custody (owner: dave)

anika: I’ll prototype the JIT flow and include example Vault policies and a minimal attestation verification script.

kate: I’ll write the audit schema — will include Syslog/HTTPS examples and sample Splunk/QRadar field mappings.

dave: I’ll work with legal on contract text and on-call to author the escalation steps.

ryan: For tracking, please open a ticket per action in the security board and tag with `BYOK-CUSTODY` and `DEDICATED`. Also mark priority P1 for contract + playbook.

sec-bot: New issue created: SEC-1227 "BYOK custody boundaries + RBAC/audit requirements" assigned to michelle, dave, anika, kate. See <https://redwood.example/SEC-1227> :robot_face:

michelle: Small detail — audit retention defaults: 1y for hosted, 3y option for enterprise. Make retention configurable per-customer and include immutable storage option (WORM).

ryan: OK sounds good. One more: rotation policy — customer rotation with Redwood-assisted rollover. We should disallow server-side automated rotations that leak plaintext to Redwood. Rotations must be staged: new_wrapped_dek -> test -> promote -> retire old. Document steps.

anika: Will include step-by-step and sample APIs for rotate_unwrap/rotate_promote endpoints. They’ll be rate-limited and require `justification` and attestation token.

kate: On incident response: add a checklist to notify customers within X hours for any key-related compromise (contract-dependent). Recommend 2-hour initial notification SLA for Dedicated with BYOK.

ryan: Great — thank you all. If no objections I’ll close this thread after tickets live. :+1:

michelle: No objections. Please include a short FAQ for customers about what we can and cannot do with BYOK keys.

ryan: Will do. Closing when SEC-1227 has all sub-tasks.
